opening_message:
Ticket 1: Nathaniel Young (employee ID E031) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E031.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Nathaniel Young (E031) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Requested write access to Payroll, which is owned by the Payroll Specialist role. Write is within the allowed level for full-time employees, so recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E031 is a contractor with basic security training (note: this conflicts with HR's full-time record). Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Basic training limits max to read. Requested write exceeds max, so recommend granting read.
reason: HR's record (authoritative for employment type) shows E031 is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, so as a full-time employee whose role owns the system, their maximum is admin. The requested level (write) is at or below that maximum, so grant write. Note: Security's record conflicts by listing the employee as a contractor with basic training; if that were the case the max would be read. I rely on HR's employment-type record, under which write is within policy and matches the request.
